speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Start with Dan. Thank you. Afternoon, Michael.  A great way to end the season. How are you  
feeling after that, and especially after the  last two weeks? Yeah, as you would imagine,  
delighted. Absolutely delighted in so many  ways with today, and particularly over the last  
two or three weeks when positions were kind of  cemented and we knew where we were in the league.  
It is easy to drift and lose a bit of momentum and  lose a bit of focus. We have kind of treated it as  
all one season going into the next one, really.  It has not ended here. I think we wanted to keep  
building and keep pushing, and credit to the  players. It is not easy sometimes to do it, as  
much as we would have expected and hoped for it.  I have been there, and it is to find that spark.  
But the hunger was there, you could see it. It  was probably the toughest team to play that type  
of game against, in the heat, the way they move  the ball. So it needed a really strong mentality,  
which I was absolutely delighted with, because  that is the foundation we need to show and have to  
give us the confidence to move forward. Talking  about moving forward, I guess it is the first  
time we have spoken to you since the contract  extension. How much are you looking forward to  
doing that at this club? Yeah, I am. I genuinely  am. It has not changed how I am. I am delighted  
I am here for longer and we need to keep  progressing, but in terms of it being a big moment  
this week for us, we just keep pushing, keep  working. I think we have done since the start.  
I have said it to you all along, really, and there  is work to do. We have got to keep improving. We  
want to be a little bit better. But it is so, so  encouraging doing it from this place, you know,  
and sharing that moment with the supporters  again at the end, I think, is important for us,  
because that is why we are here, that is why it  drives us on. Getting younger players on the pitch  
and giving them opportunities is what we are, this  club. So there are so many positives today and we  
can take that moving forward. Simon, over the  last few weeks, you have said a few times that  
it feels kind of natural almost for you, being  in the job and being at Carrington. There have  
been plenty of times that it has looked like an  impossible job managing Manchester United. Why do  
you feel so comfortable in those surroundings?  And although it does not guarantee anything,  
do you think it helps that you know the club, you  understand what makes this football club tick? I  
think it helps that I have been here for a long  time and I have seen different levels of success,  
some ups and some downs. So I have seen it  from all angles, really. I do not take that  
for granted and I do not think that just makes  the job easier. When I say it feels natural,  
again, I do not take that for granted. I think  it is trying to make the best of the situation,  
really. But I love doing it, you know, and I love  doing it. I think we have got a good idea how we  
want to move forward. We have done some good work  so far as a whole club and as a group. So, yeah,  
a lot of it is kind of what I know, all I know.  So I just keep trying to draw on those experiences  
and trying to shape how we think and how we want  it to look, really. Are you aware of the stats  
about your managerial tenure here? Thirty-nine  points from games at the end of the season should  
be enough for 87 points, I think, stretched over  a campaign. I know it is not as straightforward  
as that, but when you have that sort of bank of  work, is that something that gives you confidence,  
particularly given the fluctuations of other  rivals? I think the biggest thing you can take  
from that is the confidence and the belief that  putting results together in this league is tough,  
you know, and a run is challenging. So I  think that is the biggest thing. Obviously,  
it is a whole new start in many ways, but you  have still got to draw on it. Talking about  
experiences of being here in the past and  what it is like, I think you always draw  
on those experiences and take the positives.  The boys have to. I think they need a lot of  
credit as well as a group for how consistent  they have been in different ways we have won  
games and how strong they are knitted. I think  that is really important for us to appreciate,  
and that is what gives me the encouragement and  excitement moving forward, that we have got a  
real strong foundation now to try and build on.  Sam, I know it is the end of the season, but that  
is obviously your first game in permanent charge  and your biggest win as well. There have been some  
pretty bad days here in previous years. Do you  feel like that could be seen as you and the team  
laying down a marker for next season? We  genuinely did not treat it like that. It  
really has not changed. I half forgot that it  was the first game since I had been announced,  
really, because someone asked me about it before  the game. We were just carrying on as normal. I  
just think it gives us confidence, really, and  it gives the team confidence as much as anything.  
Whether that has an effect on others, I do not  know. But I think it is for us to draw upon when  
we get together in pre-season, the boys come back  from the World Cup, knowing that we can trust each  
other, we can work together, we can give a bit  extra for each other. When you go through that,  
I think it is quite powerful. We spoke about that  as a group. So, again, it is a place to start from  
now, moving forward. But it is nice to be able  to draw on all those emotions to give us that  
confidence. Chris, fantastic for Bruno. He has got  the record outright now. There was a lot of talk  
over his future at the club last summer. That is  well documented now. There could be more talk this  
summer. How confident are you now as head coach  that he will be with you next season, and of all  
the business that you will do this summer, how  important will he be in that? Yeah, he is such  
an influence for us, you know, and he has been the  captain and led by example in different ways. So,  
yeah, I have got no reason to think otherwise.  We have loved what he has done and he loves being  
here. I think you can see that. He wanted to stay  on. He wants to stay on every single game because  
he is enjoying his football, which is fantastic.  Last question. Hi, Michael. Some of the best  
players on the pitch there were the younger lads.  Kobbie, Patrick, Amad, all brilliant. Twenty-one,  
23, I think. Does that show you what is achievable  over the next couple of years? Although Casemiro  
has gone today, it was just as good a performance.  There was a real young nucleus there that could do  
something special over the next couple of years.  Yeah, it gives us confidence, you know, without  
getting carried away and taking anything for  granted. We have had a good spell. But I do think,  
again, experience, I keep repeating myself, but  I think, especially for the younger players,  
you cannot put a price on a season or two in  this league and playing for Manchester United,  
dealing with that and learning and understanding  what it feels like to then perform, really. The  
boys have shown that. I think Patrick especially,  it was a massive setback for him at the time  
when he got injured. But the way he has just  got on with it, I think it is incredible to  
think he is so young still, and to come back  like he did today is great. I have to say,  
I thought Mason in particular as well, playing in  midfield, I was delighted for him. I thought he  
did ever so well. Kobbie just keeps improving  all the time. All right, thanks, everyone.  
All right, guys. Cheers. Have a nice summer, huh?  Have a good summer. Cannot wait to see you again...
title: Michael Carrick post-match press conference | Brighton 0-3 Manchester United | Premier League
